propositions: Bedrock Converse and Anthropic direct reject requests with toolUse history but missing toolConfig field (provider protocol constraint); pydantic-ai's tool_step_limit mechanism hides tools via filtered() which violates this constraint mid-run after tool calls occur, causing ValidationException 400

Current tool_step_limit implementation converts valid convergence boundaries into provider errors swept into LLMUnavailableError, affecting every armed site; evidence recovery at step 17 of 16-step limit dies identically
FunctionModel tests mask the constraint because they accept tools-less requests over tool_use history offline; the provider protocol boundary is unrepresented in unit tests

Replacement mechanism wraps toolsets in WrapperToolset subclass that steers with synthetic tool results instead of hiding tools; tool definitions persist advertised for the entire run, keeping requests protocol-valid on both first-class providers

Steering is advisory so terminal bound remains the existing budget (UsageLimits with request_limit and tool_calls_limit); non-cooperative models that ignore steering still exhaust budget and raise UsageLimitExceeded as today
Live evidence: agents landed cleanly after real + steered tool calls (3+7 and 4+2) on Bedrock us-east-1 (exp_g, exp_h on 2026-08-05), proving the protocol-valid request shape works end to end
